summary: express-json-database fetches remote text from hardcoded endpoint and forwards it to undeclared `inline-array` executor
details: express-json-database 2.1.4 ships an index.js that, when `setTimestart` is invoked, performs a challenge/attest handshake against the hardcoded endpoint https://cafrino-feed.onrender.com/api/feed, reads the response body as text, and passes the resulting bytes to `inlinearray(text, true)` from a module required as `inline-array`. The package.json declares no dependencies, so `inline-array` is not resolved by installing this package; whichever module answers to that name in the host project becomes the executor for the remote text. The challenge/attest wrapper gates retrieval of the payload while the advertised 'feed' purpose carries no legitimate data (envKeys/processes are sent empty), and the loader/executor split across a hardcoded author-controlled host and an undeclared sibling module is a staged remote-code-loader shape rather than a database or feed feature.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
